class="RichText__Container-sc-39eba4fb-0 cLZCbP"><p>“Cheap Thrills” was originally released as a promo single back in December 2015, but its remix from the legendary <a href="https://genius.com/artists/Sean-paul" rel="noopener" data-api_path="/artists/740">Sean Paul</a> gave it new life. It was pushed to radio and became Sia’s first Hot 100 No. 1 as a lead artist in late July 2016.</p>

<p>“Cheap Thrills” was originally written for <a href="https://genius.com/artists/Rihanna" rel="noopener" data-api_path="/artists/89">Rihanna</a>’s <em>Anti</em> but she turned it down. Sia <a href="http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/why-rihanna-turned-down-the-number-one-song-in-the-country-w430999" rel="noopener nofollow">told <em>Rolling Stone</em></a>:</p>

<blockquote><p>I went to Greg [Kurstin, a frequent collaborator of Sia’s], and that’s what we came up with. I realized just as soon as I was cutting it that it sounded a little bit too Brit-pop for her. It’s more Icona Pop. We did actually send it to her, but they passed on it, and then I just couldn’t stop listening to it in the car.</p></blockquote>

<p>The song was nominated for numerous awards the following year including Best Pop Duo/Group Performance at the 2017 Grammy Awards. The song also earned Sia her first ever Pop Work of the Year at 2017 APRA Awards.</p></div></div><div class="ExpandableContent__ButtonContainer-sc-c79fe528-3 iaYeGE"><button type="button" <p>“Cheap Thrills” isn’t the first hit song of 2016 to use patois in its lyrics—Rihanna’s <a href="https://genius.com/Rihanna-work-lyrics" rel="noopener" data-api_path="/songs/2398213">“Work”</a> was
